transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has said he feels he can work with the incoming Democratic majority next
year in Congress.
He was asked by CBS's 60 Minutes program, which aired yesterday, if he thought his mass
deportation programs were too severe and whether they might have cost Republicans midterm elections.
Do you think your deportation policy went too far?
It was too tough.
I think it might be too tough, yeah.
What would happen?
What does the deal look like with the Democrats?
I think ultimately that hurt me.
Well, the deal would be we would work something out, and I think it's something, I think that's
something that's actually doable.
That interview with CBS was recorded last Friday.
However, Trump also decided to name his new White House chief of staff last Friday, Stephen
Miller.
And today is Miller's first day on the job.
Miller has led Trump's most draconian immigration efforts, including mass deportations.
Democratic lawmakers have expressed astonishment.
They say they will forcefully push back on any extremism.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in Paris for meetings with G7 foreign ministers.
NPR's Rebecca Rossman reports Iran and Ukraine are expected to be major topics.
The latest two-day meeting of allies kicks off today in Paris.
The talks begin as Rubio's G7 counterparts face uncertainty about how last week's midterm
defeat might affect the Trump administration's foreign policy approach.
Major topics on the agenda include the Iran conflict and ending the war in Ukraine.
The meeting coincides with separate U.S.-mediated peace talks between Moscow and Kiev in Abu
Dhabi.
The French foreign minister says Europe will be a part of those talks, but it wasn't immediately
clear how the bloc would be represented.
Ukrainian governments have said they're concerned the U.S. might be pushing Ukraine for a deal
that would favor Russia.
Rebecca Rossman and Pierre Neus, Paris.
Ukrainians say they don't place much stock in the latest round of peace negotiations
hosted by the Trump administration in Abu Dhabi this week.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Ukrainians say nothing will change, as long as Russian
President Putin keeps his demands.
Oleksandr Merezhko, chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Ukrainian Parliament,
says there will be no results.
"It's very easy to predict for a very simple reason.
Because Putin is not interested in negotiating or making any kind of compromise."
In an interview on CBS's 60 Minutes Sunday night, President Trump said a deal is very
near and no one's been tougher on Russia than him.
Merezhko says Russia plans to weaponize this fifth winter of war to freeze Ukrainians into
submission.
"The problem is that Putin is using these negotiations, actually he's imitating negotiations
with only one purpose, to avoid sanctions from Trump."
But Ukrainians will play along, he says, so as not to be considered spoilers.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Officials at Big Tech computer chip maker Nvidia are investigating their own CEO.
They say Jensen Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort."
Published reports say Huang is suspected of having a romantic relationship with a woman
who is an alleged Chinese spy.
NPR has not confirmed this reporting.
Nvidia published a memo Huang wrote to employees where he admits and apologizes for his role
in the relationship.
Meanwhile, China is denying any role in any spying matter.
Reservoirs in the southwestern U.S. have gotten a boost from recent rounds of heavy rain.
NPR's Rebecca Herscher has more.
Many reservoirs in the southwest were running dangerously low over the summer because of
a multi-year mega-drought in the region.
Such droughts are more likely because of climate change.
The reservoirs provide water for drinking, irrigation, and industry.
The most famous is Lake Powell, which is the second largest reservoir in the U.S.
It reached record low levels in September.
But rainstorms in October and November brought much needed water to the region, even as the
storms caused major flood damage in some places.
The water level in Lake Powell is now 20 feet higher than it was in late September, although
it is still far from being full.
Rebecca Herscher, NPR News.
Pope Leo is in Argentina on his South American visit.
He is expected to celebrate mass outdoors today in Buenos Aires.
Reuters News Agency reports that well over one million people may attend.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
This message comes from Rince.
A well-designed life doesn't run on default settings.
You chose the walkable neighborhood, your coffee order became oddly specific, you spent
three weeks choosing your mattress.
But your laundry routine?
That one somehow escaped the redesign.
Should that really be the one update you skipped?
Consider this the patch.
Rince picks up your laundry and dry cleaning, cleans it expertly, and delivers it back.
Sign up today at rince.com.
Rince, it's time to be great.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Trump says Democrats' incoming House majority could work together, after deportations 'too tough' remark on 60 Minutes
Trump names Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff; Democrats vow pushback on his immigration record
Secretary of State Rubio attends G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris on Iran and Ukraine
Ukrainians doubt latest U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi will produce results
Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged romantic ties to suspected Chinese spy; China denies involvement
Heavy rains lift southwestern U.S. reservoirs, including Lake Powell, after record-low levels in September
Pope Leo begins South American visit in Argentina with outdoor mass in Buenos Aires expected to draw crowds
